channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Hunt-Fike rivalry reignites as playoff picture sharpens
item.description: As Hunt and Fike renew their rivalry with Big East lead and RPI on the line, Wilson-area powers from Wilson Prep to Greenfield and Community Christian jostle for rankings, titles and playoff position across every classification.

item.title: Breakfast keeps King’s message alive
item.description: At Wilson's 32nd Ecumenical Prayer Breakfast, speakers honored Martin Luther King Jr.'s legacy, urging personal responsibility, faith-rooted peace and renewed commitment to justice in a polarized nation.

item.title: Wingstop opens to a crowd in Wilson
item.description: Wingstop’s surprise soft launch draws crowds in Wilson as the chain opens at 3401 Raleigh Road Parkway W., hiring local staff and extending Legacy Wings’ North Carolina expansion.

item.title: Our Opinion: Wilson council should reconsider video blackout
item.description: An emotional plea to protect Vick Cemetery was kept off-air by Wilson’s longstanding ban on broadcasting public comments, renewing criticism of a policy seen as undermining transparency.

item.title: Recipe vs. result: Does the US government actually exist?
item.description: A libertarian columnist argues the U.S. government described in the Constitution does not exist, using a recipe metaphor to question whether “constitutional government” is even possible.

item.title: Harrigan’s manipulative, anti-urban populism
item.description: A North Carolina policy analyst argues Rep. Pat Harrigan’s anti-immigrant, anti-urban rhetoric revives nativist populist tropes while pushing policies that undercut his own working-class district.

item.title: Liberty and generosity form virtuous circle
item.description: Evidence links economic freedom with greater charity, trust and tolerance, forming a virtuous circle that guides the Pope Foundation’s philanthropy and underscores the need for liberty grounded in strong social institutions.

item.title: Kids like me are proving democracy isn’t just for adults
item.description: A ninth grader from Alaska, newly crowned 2024 National Civics Bee champion, shares how personal health struggles led her to lobby Congress and show that young people can help shape U.S. democracy through civics.

item.title: What’s next, America?
item.description: An 81-year-old Pikeville resident condemns Trump's foreign ventures, fears they could bring war home and urges leaders to refocus on U.S. needs and rein in the presidency.
